assessment: A cover that locates itself on different corner profiles is conceivable, but neither its durability nor batch feasibility is established. The supplied failures motivate testing corner accommodation without assuming it explains the large-cover rework.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: corner pockets with short, concealed elastic gathering could seat the printed cover against the tabletop while accommodating modest corner-radius differences without repeated adjustment.
openings.delta: Replace fixed corner capture with compliant capture. Dependencies are sufficient panel dimensions, balanced tension, washable elastic and seams, unobstructed table undersides, and preserved visible design. Presently testable partial capability: determine whether a gathered offcut corner can seat consistently on square and rounded corners.
openings.prediction: With panel dimensions held constant, compliant pockets would reduce placement failures on rounded corners relative to fixed pockets, without introducing puckering or square-corner failures.
openings.probe: Use retained offcuts for paired corner mockups and seek a rounded-table trial from the six willing customers. Compare repeated placements with fixed pockets, then repeat after the stipulated wash test. Before stock cutting, cost materials and labor, verify the three-week schedule, and calculate cutting waste by area; advance only within 350 units and 8% waste.
assumptions: Suitable elastic is affordable and obtainable.
Corner capture contributes to the observed installation failures.
Required compliance does not distort the ordered design.

openings.claim: Do large-cover failures originate in panel size before corner capture, making compliant pockets insufficient?
openings.delta: Distinguish a whole-panel dimension deficit from a localized corner-seating problem.
openings.prediction: A panel deficit produces tension or shortfall across straight edges even with corners temporarily released; a corner-capture problem improves when only the pockets are released.
openings.probe: On the first medium and large covers, use temporary corner stitching and record straight-edge fit before and after releasing the pockets. Record actual tabletop dimensions, cutting direction and operator; include this trial labor in batch timing.
assumptions: Temporary stitching can be removed without damaging the purchased cloth.
